_comment: The request-id / correlation-id contract: ONE answer key, four frameworks. Feature 43.
Every request carries a correlation id: an inbound X-Request-ID is HONOURED
when it is well-formed, else one is GENERATED; the id is ECHOED on the
response X-Request-ID header and threaded into every log line for the
request. The inbound value is SANITIZED first (allow-list charset
[A-Za-z0-9._-], length cap 128, CR/LF and every other control char rejected)
so an attacker-controlled header can never inject a second response header or
forge a log line - RID-DEC-02. Before this feature the full behaviour existed
ONLY in Python (with two live defects); PHP minted one id PER PROCESS, and
Ruby/Node had the setter but never called it in the request path. RID-DEC-01
(OWNER-DECIDED 2026-08-11) built it in all four - see
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/OWNER-DECISIONS.md and
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/features/043-request-id.md.
Every case is driven through the REAL request pipeline - Python's TestClient
and PHP/Ruby TestClients dispatch through the real front controller; Node
boots a REAL server and makes REAL HTTP requests over a socket - with NO
mocks. The logger case reads a REAL log file the framework wrote. The witness
is a real side effect: the response X-Request-ID header, the id the handler
reads back, and the [id] in a log line the framework wrote to disk.
The four suites carry the SAME case names in each language's idiom (Python
snake_case method, PHP testPascalCase method, Ruby it-description, Node assert
label), which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py normalises and matches. Each
framework also carries request-scoped storage tests (Python contextvars, Ruby
thread-local, Node AsyncLocalStorage, PHP per-request) that are NOT in this
shared set because the concurrency mechanism differs per runtime.

invariants.rule: A well-formed inbound X-Request-ID ([A-Za-z0-9._-], 1..128 chars) is HONOURED - the same id is echoed on the response X-Request-ID header AND read back by the handler for this request - so a client or an upstream service can thread its own correlation id through the app.
invariants.why: A correlation id is only useful end to end if the app respects the one the caller already assigned. Before RID-DEC-01 only Python honoured the inbound header; PHP/Ruby/Node ignored it, so a downstream trace id was silently dropped in three of four.
cases: inbound id is honoured and echoed

invariants.rule: When no inbound X-Request-ID is sent, the framework GENERATES a well-formed id ([A-Za-z0-9._-], 1..128 chars) and echoes it on the response X-Request-ID header - and the handler reads back the SAME id.
invariants.why: Every request must be correlatable whether or not the caller supplied an id. Before RID-DEC-01 PHP generated one id per PROCESS (useless under the long-running server) and Ruby/Node put no id on the wire at all.
cases: absent id is generated and echoed

invariants.rule: A hostile inbound X-Request-ID is SANITIZED before it is used: a value carrying CR/LF, one longer than 128 chars, or one with any character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] is rejected wholesale and a fresh id is generated - so the raw value NEVER reflects into the response header or a log line. Mutation-proved: disabling the sanitizer reflects the raw value into the response X-Request-ID header (proven live in all four).
invariants.why: The inbound header is attacker-controlled. Reflecting it raw into a response header is HTTP response-splitting (a CR/LF forges a second header, e.g. Set-Cookie) and into a log line is log injection - RID-PY-INJECTION, which was a LIVE defect in Python and would have been reintroduced by naively wiring the dormant setter in Ruby/Node. CR/LF cannot travel intact over a compliant HTTP client (the transport itself blocks it), so Node proves the CR/LF case at the sanitizer function; the over-long and illegal-charset cases travel over real HTTP in every framework.

invariants.rule: A log line written while serving the request CARRIES the request's id: the framework writes the id into every log line (text form [<id>], JSON form request_id) so logs for one request are correlatable and match the id echoed on the response. Witnessed by reading a REAL log file the framework wrote and finding the request's id on the marker line.
invariants.why: Log correlation is the whole point of a request id. Before RID-DEC-01 Ruby and Node never called the setter in the request path, so get_request_id was nil during a real request and no log line carried an id; PHP's one process id made every request's lines look identical.
cases: log line carries the request id
